summary: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship pays full tuition for year one, plus a contribution to living costs, for top international students on a two-year regular MSc at TU Delft. Year two continues if you earn at least 48 ECTS in year one. Only about 16 are awarded (two per faculty) to applicants in roughly the top 10% of their class.
lookfor: Academic excellence: about the top 10% of your previous programme
What makes you excellent beyond grades: activities and wider interests
Why TU Delft and the specific MSc, and why you need the scholarship
How you would contribute to your MSc programme
cycle: MSc applications open 15 October 2026. For the scholarship, your complete MSc application, the Scholarship Application Form and one reference letter must be in by 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET. Decisions are emailed by the end of March 2027.

eligibility.q: Are you an international applicant to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc (not an International Joint Education Programme)?
eligibility.no: Choose a regular two-year MSc, or consider Erasmus Mundus programmes for joint degrees.

eligibility.q: Are you in about the top 10% of your bachelor's class?
eligibility.no: Consider less selective awards such as Erasmus Mundus or the Swedish Institute scholarship.

eligibility.q: Do you meet TU Delft's degree rule for your country (for Nigeria: a five-year bachelor's with First Class or Second Class Upper)?
eligibility.no: Check the 'where did you obtain your degree' page; if you do not meet it you cannot be admitted.

eligibility.q: Will you be 35 or younger on 1 September 2027?
eligibility.no: TU Delft's FAQ sets this age limit; look at awards without age caps.

eligibility.q: Can you complete the full MSc application, including an English test, by 1 December 2026?
eligibility.no: If you cannot, prepare for the next round, which opens in October each year.

steps.title: Confirm the MSc and the rules
steps.why: With only about 16 awards, you must be clearly eligible and in a strong-fit programme.
do: Open the TU Delft scholarships page and read the Justus & Louise van Effen section.
Open the 'where did you obtain your degree' page and check your country's rule.
Choose your two-year MSc programme and read its admission page.
Read the scholarship FAQ (age limit, reference letter).
tips: Awards are split two per faculty, so you compete within your faculty.
avoid: Choosing a programme that needs GRE without time to take it.
check: I meet the degree, grade and age rules.

steps.title: Build a tight seven-week timeline
steps.why: The scholarship deadline (1 December) is much earlier than the normal MSc deadline.
do: Mark 15 October 2026 (applications open) and 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET (scholarship deadline).
Set your own deadline of 24 November.
Book your English test now so results arrive by mid-November.
Ask your referee this week.
tips: Write the motivation letter and form answers in parallel; they overlap.
avoid: Planning around the April MSc deadline.

steps.title: Register on Studielink and the TU Delft portal
steps.why: Your scholarship is only considered with a complete MSc application.
do: Register on Studielink and choose your MSc.
Wait for your TU Delft NetID email (up to 24 hours).
Log in to the TU Delft application portal and open the document upload list.
Pay the EUR 100 application fee.
avoid: Leaving the fee unpaid — the application is not complete without it.
check: I can see my application and upload list.

steps.title: Get official transcripts and degree certificate
steps.why: TU Delft does not accept unofficial transcripts.
do: Request official transcripts and your certificate from your university registry.
Get certified English translations if not in English.
Scan clearly and upload.
Check that your CGPA meets the requirement without rounding.
tips: If still studying, upload your latest official transcript.
avoid: Expecting updated transcripts later to change the decision — they are not considered.

steps.title: Take your English test
steps.why: Scholarship applicants must include an English test certificate.
do: Book TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, or Cambridge C1/C2 now.
Check your programme's minimum score.
Upload the result with its verification number.
Make sure the test is less than two years old when you submit.
tips: Book the earliest date you can be ready for; rescheduling is costly.

steps.title: Write your CV
steps.why: Your CV supports the 'excellence beyond grades' question.
do: Write an English CV of maximum three pages.
Include education, research, work, awards, leadership and activities in chronological order.
Upload as PDF.
tips: List class rank or 'top x%' if your university can confirm it.
check: My CV is three pages or fewer.

steps.title: Write the MSc motivation letter
steps.why: Admission depends on it, and scholarship selection happens only after admission.
do: Explain why this programme and why TU Delft.
State your expectations and preferred specialisation.
Propose three possible thesis topics.
Add a summary of your bachelor's thesis (max 250 words) including workload.
Keep within 1,000–1,500 words.
tips: Name research groups or professors linked to your thesis ideas.
check: All required parts are covered within the word range.
steps.prompt: Why this programme and TU Delft, your expectations, specialisation, three thesis topics, and a bachelor's thesis summary.

steps.title: Complete the Scholarship Application Form
steps.why: This two-page form is where you show excellence and fit for the scholarship.
do: Download the 2027–2029 Scholarship Application Form.
Introduce yourself (100 words).
What makes you excellent besides grades (150 words).
Why TU Delft and why the scholarship (200 words).
How you would contribute to your MSc programme (200 words).
Career plans after graduation (200 words).
Keep the whole form to two A4 pages; upload as PDF.
tips: Use different examples from the motivation letter so you add new evidence.
avoid: Exceeding word limits or the two-page limit.
check: Each answer is within its limit.
steps.prompt: Five questions: introduce yourself; excellence beyond grades; why TU Delft and the scholarship; your contribution to the MSc; career plans.

steps.title: Get one strong reference letter
steps.why: One reference letter is required for scholarship applicants.
do: Ask a former professor or employer who knows your work well.
Send your CV, programme link and points to mention (class rank, research).
Ask for English or Dutch, on letterhead, signed and stamped.
Upload it as one PDF; if you have two letters, combine them into one PDF.
tips: A letter stating you are in the top 10% is valuable evidence.

steps.title: Submit everything before 1 December
steps.why: Late or incomplete applications are not considered for the scholarship.
do: Check every required document is uploaded.
Confirm the fee is paid.
Submit the application.
Save the confirmation.
tips: Contact scholarships-esa@tudelft.nl if something is unclear.
check: My application is submitted and complete.

steps.title: Wait for admission and scholarship results
steps.why: Scholarship selection happens after conditional or full admission.
do: Watch email for your admission decision.
Expect the scholarship decision by the end of March 2027.
If awarded, accept and follow visa instructions (TU Delft applies for the Dutch residence permit).
tips: Plan for year two: you need 48 ECTS in year one.
avoid: Accepting another scholarship — they cannot be combined.
check: I know my result and next steps.

faq.q: Do I need a separate scholarship portal?
faq.a: No. You upload the form and reference letter with your MSc application.
TU Delft's FAQ says you must be 35 or younger on 1 September of your first year.

faq.q: Can I combine it with another scholarship?

faq.a: Yes, if you earn at least 48 ECTS in year one.
